The iOS podspec keeps `s.vendored_frameworks` (and iOS statically links it — building the framework's code into the app). The macOS one removed it entirely, so the pod target's EnforceBundling.swift (which references ~200 FRB symbols + dummy_method_to_enforce_bundling from the static archive) no longer links.

Wait — but did the macOS podspec's EnforceBundling compile before? Yes — it linked against the vendored dynamic framework which contained those symbols.

Now what's the right fix consistent with the PR's intent (drop the 27 MB framework from the shipped app, keep FFI working via dlsym on executable with force-loaded static archive)?

Options:

**Option A**: Keep the pod target compiling by linking the static archive into the pod target instead of vendoring the framework: `s.vendored_libraries = "Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a"`. But that would statically link all frb symbols into the pod framework — and the pod framework would still be shipped (it's a source-built framework from source_files, tiny — just EnforceBundling). Hmm, but then the framework would export duplicate symbols of the force-loaded app archive. Duplicates between app executable and dylib are fine at runtime (two-level namespace, app exports take precedence for dlsym on executable? Actually dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT) searches... DynamicLibrary.executable() looks up in the executable's exported symbols table. Duplicates in a dylib don't break that). But it does duplicate code into the shipped framework (small-ish? the static archive is how big? 27MB dynamic framework included the rust static lib; the archive likely several MB). That defeats the size diet partially.

**Option B**: Remove EnforceBundling from the macOS plugin build. Why does EnforceBundling exist? It's the standard flutter_rust_bridge pattern: dummy method referencing all generated symbols so the linker doesn't strip them. On iOS it matters because the static archive is linked into the app and dead-code elimination might strip unused wire symbols. On macOS, the app force_loads the whole archive and exports _wire_* symbols, so the dummy isn't needed. If the pod target has no source files... but a pod with no source_files may fail. Actually the plugin also has frb.h header (public_header_files). Could set s.source_files to nothing meaningful? Pods require at least something? Actually a podspec with empty source_files might be OK (resource-less pod). But the header is public API... The header is included via package's ffi? The Dart side uses DynamicLibrary directly, not the plugin's C API. The Classes/frb.h is the C header for ffigen on the Dart side maybe.

Hmm — but wait, does the Runner force_load + export only apply to Release? The PR says force_load applies to release and dev builds. Let me check the Runner.xcodeproj and Podfile to understand the linking setup, and how the symbols get exported. Also check the "wasm_run FFI symbol verification" CI step.

**Option C**: Make the podspec not build EnforceBundling on macOS: move EnforceBundling.swift out of macos/Classes (it's in macos/Classes). The ios podspec has its own Classes dir? ios/ likely has its own Classes with its own EnforceBundling. Let me check.

        done

        if [ -f "${LITERTLM}" ]; then
          install_name_tool -change \\
            @rpath/libGemmaModelConstraintProvider.dylib \\
            @rpath/GemmaModelConstraintProvider.framework/Versions/A/GemmaModelConstraintProvider \\
            "${LITERTLM}" 2>/dev/null || true

        fi

        touch "${SCRIPT_OUTPUT_FILE_0}"

    end
  end

  # wasm_run FFI symbols live in a static library inside WasmRun.xcframework.
  # They are referenced only from Dart via dlsym (DynamicLibrary.executable()),
  # so the linker never pulls them in: force_load alone is not enough because
  # DEAD_CODE_STRIPPING=YES (Release default) still discards the unreferenced
  # code, and dlsym only sees exported symbols. Exporting a symbol makes it
  # both dlsym-visible AND a dead-strip root, so export every C-ABI symbol the
  # Dart bindings look up (wire_*/new_*/drop_*/…), derived from the archive
  # itself so the list stays in sync with the vendored package. Without this
  # the Release/TestFlight binary boots to a white screen. SRCROOT is the
  # macos/ directory, so ../../ walks up to the repo root where vendor/ lives.
  macos_slice = '$(SRCROOT)/../../vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a'
  macos_archive = File.expand_path('../../vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a', __dir__)
  ffi_symbols = `nm -gU -arch arm64 #{macos_archive}`.lines
    .map(&:split)
    .select { |cols| %w[T D S].include?(cols[1]) && cols[2] }
    .map { |cols| cols[2] }
    .uniq
    .grep(/^_(wire|new|drop|free|get|store|init|inflate|share)_/)
    .sort
  raise "no wasm_run FFI symbols found in #{macos_archive}" if ffi_symbols.empty?
  export_flags = ffi_symbols.map { |s| "-Wl,-exported_symbol,#{s}" }
  installer.aggregate_targets.each do |aggregate_target|
    aggregate_target.user_project.targets.each do |target|
      next unless target.name == 'Runner'
      target.build_configurations.each do |config|
        # Archive/install builds run `strip` per STRIP_STYLE. The default
        # "all" removes the dyld exports trie entirely, which kills the
        # dlsym-based wasm_run lookups at runtime — TestFlight white screen.
        # "non-global" (strip -x) keeps the trie intact.
        config.build_settings['STRIP_STYLE'] = 'non-global'
        ldflags = Array(config.build_settings['OTHER_LDFLAGS'] || ['$(inherited)']).dup
        # Drop stale wasm_run flags from earlier pod installs.
        ldflags.reject! { |f| f == '-force_load' || f.include?('wasm_run_dart.a') || f.start_with?('-Wl,-exported_symbol,') }
        ldflags << "-Wl,-force_load,#{macos_slice}"
        # Debug must NOT get -exported_symbol flags: giving any flips ld
        # into "export only these" mode, which hides the JIT entry point
        # (main) from the debug host — abort_could_not_find_entry_point
        # at launch. Debug exports all globals by default, so dlsym finds
        # the wire_* symbols without any flags.
        ldflags.concat(export_flags) unless config.name == 'Debug'
        config.build_settings['OTHER_LDFLAGS'] = ldflags
      end
    end
    aggregate_target.user_project.save
  end
end

running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.

## PR Description

Part of #1096 — slice 2: the cuts slice 1 explicitly deferred (AC4 + direction-3 analog on macOS, owner-decision items untouched). Budget-gate script unchanged; baselines reseeded onto the measured post-cut shape.

## Delivered

### AC4 — macOS app ships without `wasm_run_flutter.framework` (27.1 MB unpacked)
`vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/wasm_run_flutter.podspec`: `s.vendored_frameworks` removed. The embedded dynamic framework was a **never-loaded fallback**: the Dart FFI surface resolves via dlsym on the app's own executable — `Runner.xcodeproj` force_loads `WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a` and exports the `_wire_*` symbols (verified per build by the existing `wasm_run FFI symbol verification` step). `createLibraryImpl` (`vendor/wasm_run/lib/src/ffi/io.dart:50-56`) tries `DynamicLibrary.executable()` first on macOS and `_validateLibrary` checks exactly `wire_compile_wasm` — the symbol the CI gate asserts. So `WasmRunLibrary.setUp(override: false)` no-ops on the pruned build; **no Dart change, no boot-time dylib download**. The XCFramework cache/restore/download stays untouched — the static archive feeds the force_load and the Podfile symbol check (`Podfile:132-141`); `wasmrun_restore_budget_test` stays green (5/5).

### macOS flutter_assets diet (direction 3 analog, ~52 MB unpacked)
`build-macos.yml` Package step prunes, **before any codesign**:
- `flutter_assets/assets/wasm` — ~47 MB of WASI interpreter modules loaded exclusively through `WasiSandboxShell` (`env_factory_io.dart` routes desktops to the host `Process` shell; every `rootBundle.load('assets/wasm/…')` lives in the mobile-only shell — re-verified on current main). Mobile (iOS/Android) builds untouched — they keep the full set (backward-compat invariant).
- `flutter_assets/packages/js_widget_runtime/test` — 5.6 MB coach_anny.glb test fixture of the pub package, declared as package assets; nothing in the app references that path (grep over flutter_app/lib, packages, lib, bundled JS apps).

### Same fixture prune on every other shipped web shape (5.6 MB each)
`scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` (extension zip), `.github/workflows/pages.yml` (fa1.dev), `scripts/build_office_addin.sh` (outlook pane).

### AC1 ratchet — baselines reseeded onto the post-cut shape
Both `scripts/size_budget` floors rewritten from the **real v1.0.504 release artifacts** with the cuts applied (`--reseed`; script unchanged):
- mac zip: TOTAL 203,341,721 → 111,001,004 B unpacked (**−45.3%**); compressed auto-update zip 75.8 MB → 41.0 MB (**−46%**). DMG shrinks identically.
- extension: TOTAL 78,149,373 → 72,527,489 B (**−7.1%**); compressed 28.3 → 26.4 MB.

Gate proofs (all against the committed floors):
- cut mac zip vs pre-PR baseline: PASS (TOTAL −45.3%, no line grew) — the cut ships green even before the reseed lands
- pre-cut v1.0.504 mac zip vs new floor: **FAIL** — 4 NEW >5% lines (`wasm_run_flutter.framework` 27.1 MB, `python.wasm` 30.4 MB, `coreutils.wasm` 8.4 MB, `coach_anny.glb` 5.6 MB), TOTAL +83.2%
- pre-cut extension vs new floor: **FAIL** — glb NEW >5%, TOTAL +7.8%
- tampered cut zip (main binary +10%): **FAIL** (GREW)
- `size_manifest.py selftest`: 11/11 PASS
- per-line shapes of both cut zips otherwise byte-identical to the shipped releases (only the cut lines + engine-bump drift between v1.0.493 baselines and v1.0.504)

### Not needed (verified, deliberately no diff)
- No `wasm_setup_io.dart` change: with the framework gone, `setUp(override:false)` → `isReachable()` → `executable()` succeeds (static link + exported symbols, CI-gated) → early return. The download path never runs on release or dev builds (force_load applies to both).
- iOS podspec untouched — iOS vendors its own framework slice and statically links it.

## Remaining (owner decisions / later slices, unchanged from the issue)
- AC5: iOS lite flavor vs accept-35 MB (LiteRT/Gemma on-device stack, 35 MB iOS / 45 MB macOS)
- OQ3: `--wasm` (skwasm) spike; App.framework 89–92 MB code-size audit (direction 6)
- mac canvaskit rev-dir inner mirror (web-only shape; needs network trace before cutting — extension/web floors already carry it)
- Known gate floor: NEW-line share is 5% of TOTAL — a future single line under that (e.g. a small asset) regrows silently; the TOTAL line still covers aggregate drift.

## CI note
Per fleet policy this PR does not dispatch or rerun workflows; SM schedules CI.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan

  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text

running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.

# Pull Request Information

- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +48
- **Deletions**: -28
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T13:54:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T14:17:29Z

## PR Description

Part of #1096 — slice 2: the cuts slice 1 explicitly deferred (AC4 + direction-3 analog on macOS, owner-decision items untouched). Budget-gate script unchanged; baselines reseeded onto the measured post-cut shape.

## Delivered

### AC4 — macOS app ships without `wasm_run_flutter.framework` (27.1 MB unpacked)
`vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/wasm_run_flutter.podspec`: `s.vendored_frameworks` removed. The embedded dynamic framework was a **never-loaded fallback**: the Dart FFI surface resolves via dlsym on the app's own executable — `Runner.xcodeproj` force_loads `WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a` and exports the `_wire_*` symbols (verified per build by the existing `wasm_run FFI symbol verification` step). `createLibraryImpl` (`vendor/wasm_run/lib/src/ffi/io.dart:50-56`) tries `DynamicLibrary.executable()` first on macOS and `_validateLibrary` checks exactly `wire_compile_wasm` — the symbol the CI gate asserts. So `WasmRunLibrary.setUp(override: false)` no-ops on the pruned build; **no Dart change, no boot-time dylib download**. The XCFramework cache/restore/download stays untouched — the static archive feeds the force_load and the Podfile symbol check (`Podfile:132-141`); `wasmrun_restore_budget_test` stays green (5/5).

### macOS flutter_assets diet (direction 3 analog, ~52 MB unpacked)
`build-macos.yml` Package step prunes, **before any codesign**:
- `flutter_assets/assets/wasm` — ~47 MB of WASI interpreter modules loaded exclusively through `WasiSandboxShell` (`env_factory_io.dart` routes desktops to the host `Process` shell; every `rootBundle.load('assets/wasm/…')` lives in the mobile-only shell — re-verified on current main). Mobile (iOS/Android) builds untouched — they keep the full set (backward-compat invariant).
- `flutter_assets/packages/js_widget_runtime/test` — 5.6 MB coach_anny.glb test fixture of the pub package, declared as package assets; nothing in the app references that path (grep over flutter_app/lib, packages, lib, bundled JS apps).

### Same fixture prune on every other shipped web shape (5.6 MB each)
`scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` (extension zip), `.github/workflows/pages.yml` (fa1.dev), `scripts/build_office_addin.sh` (outlook pane).

### AC1 ratchet — baselines reseeded onto the post-cut shape
Both `scripts/size_budget` floors rewritten from the **real v1.0.504 release artifacts** with the cuts applied (`--reseed`; script unchanged):
- mac zip: TOTAL 203,341,721 → 111,001,004 B unpacked (**−45.3%**); compressed auto-update zip 75.8 MB → 41.0 MB (**−46%**). DMG shrinks identically.
- extension: TOTAL 78,149,373 → 72,527,489 B (**−7.1%**); compressed 28.3 → 26.4 MB.

Gate proofs (all against the committed floors):
- cut mac zip vs pre-PR baseline: PASS (TOTAL −45.3%, no line grew) — the cut ships green even before the reseed lands
- pre-cut v1.0.504 mac zip vs new floor: **FAIL** — 4 NEW >5% lines (`wasm_run_flutter.framework` 27.1 MB, `python.wasm` 30.4 MB, `coreutils.wasm` 8.4 MB, `coach_anny.glb` 5.6 MB), TOTAL +83.2%
- pre-cut extension vs new floor: **FAIL** — glb NEW >5%, TOTAL +7.8%
- tampered cut zip (main binary +10%): **FAIL** (GREW)
- `size_manifest.py selftest`: 11/11 PASS
- per-line shapes of both cut zips otherwise byte-identical to the shipped releases (only the cut lines + engine-bump drift between v1.0.493 baselines and v1.0.504)

### Not needed (verified, deliberately no diff)
- No `wasm_setup_io.dart` change: with the framework gone, `setUp(override:false)` → `isReachable()` → `executable()` succeeds (static link + exported symbols, CI-gated) → early return. The download path never runs on release or dev builds (force_load applies to both).
- iOS podspec untouched — iOS vendors its own framework slice and statically links it.

## Remaining (owner decisions / later slices, unchanged from the issue)
- AC5: iOS lite flavor vs accept-35 MB (LiteRT/Gemma on-device stack, 35 MB iOS / 45 MB macOS)
- OQ3: `--wasm` (skwasm) spike; App.framework 89–92 MB code-size audit (direction 6)
- mac canvaskit rev-dir inner mirror (web-only shape; needs network trace before cutting — extension/web floors already carry it)
- Known gate floor: NEW-line share is 5% of TOTAL — a future single line under that (e.g. a small asset) regrows silently; the TOTAL line still covers aggregate drift.

## CI note
Per fleet policy this PR does not dispatch or rerun workflows; SM schedules CI.

### AC4 — macOS app ships without `wasm_run_flutter.framework` (27.1 MB unpacked)
`vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/wasm_run_flutter.podspec`: `s.vendored_frameworks` removed. The embedded dynamic framework was a **never-loaded fallback**: the Dart FFI surface resolves via dlsym on the app's own executable — `Runner.xcodeproj` force_loads `WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a` and exports the `_wire_*` symbols (verified per build by the existing `wasm_run FFI symbol verification` step). `createLibraryImpl` (`vendor/wasm_run/lib/src/ffi/io.dart:50-56`) tries `DynamicLibrary.executable()` first on macOS and `_validateLibrary` checks exactly `wire_compile_wasm` — the symbol the CI gate asserts. So `WasmRunLibrary.setUp(override: false)` no-ops on the pruned build; **no Dart change, no boot-time dylib download**. The XCFramework cache/restore/download stays untouched — the static archive feeds the force_load and the Podfile symbol check (`Podfile:132-141`); `wasmrun_restore_budget_test` stays green (5/5).

### macOS flutter_assets diet (direction 3 analog, ~52 MB unpacked)
`build-macos.yml` Package step prunes, **before any codesign**:
- `flutter_assets/assets/wasm` — ~47 MB of WASI interpreter modules loaded exclusively through `WasiSandboxShell` (`env_factory_io.dart` routes desktops to the host `Process` shell; every `rootBundle.load('assets/wasm/…')` lives in the mobile-only shell — re-verified on current main). Mobile (iOS/Android) builds untouched — they keep the full set (backward-compat invariant).
- `flutter_assets/packages/js_widget_runtime/test` — 5.6 MB coach_anny.glb test fixture of the pub package, declared as package assets; nothing in the app references that path (grep over flutter_app/lib, packages, lib, bundled JS apps).

### Same fixture prune on every other shipped web shape (5.6 MB each)
`scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` (extension zip), `.github/workflows/pages.yml` (fa1.dev), `scripts/build_office_addin.sh` (outlook pane).

### AC1 ratchet — baselines reseeded onto the post-cut shape
Both `scripts/size_budget` floors rewritten from the **real v1.0.504 release artifacts** with the cuts applied (`--reseed`; script unchanged):
- mac zip: TOTAL 203,341,721 → 111,001,004 B unpacked (**−45.3%**); compressed auto-update zip 75.8 MB → 41.0 MB (**−46%**). DMG shrinks identically.
- extension: TOTAL 78,149,373 → 72,527,489 B (**−7.1%**); compressed 28.3 → 26.4 MB.

Gate proofs (all against the committed floors):
- cut mac zip vs pre-PR baseline: PASS (TOTAL −45.3%, no line grew) — the cut ships green even before the reseed lands
- pre-cut v1.0.504 mac zip vs new floor: **FAIL** — 4 NEW >5% lines (`wasm_run_flutter.framework` 27.1 MB, `python.wasm` 30.4 MB, `coreutils.wasm` 8.4 MB, `coach_anny.glb` 5.6 MB), TOTAL +83.2%
- pre-cut extension vs new floor: **FAIL** — glb NEW >5%, TOTAL +7.8%
- tampered cut zip (main binary +10%): **FAIL** (GREW)
- `size_manifest.py selftest`: 11/11 PASS
- per-line shapes of both cut zips otherwise byte-identical to the shipped releases (only the cut lines + engine-bump drift between v1.0.493 baselines and v1.0.504)

### Not needed (verified, deliberately no diff)
- No `wasm_setup_io.dart` change: with the framework gone, `setUp(override:false)` → `isReachable()` → `executable()` succeeds (static link + exported symbols, CI-gated) → early return. The download path never runs on release or dev builds (force_load applies to both).
- iOS podspec untouched — iOS vendors its own framework slice and statically links it.

  # wasm_run FFI symbols live in a static library inside WasmRun.xcframework.
  # They are referenced only from Dart via dlsym (DynamicLibrary.executable()),
  # so the linker never pulls them in: force_load alone is not enough because
  # DEAD_CODE_STRIPPING=YES (Release default) still discards the unreferenced
  # code, and dlsym only sees exported symbols. Exporting a symbol makes it
  # both dlsym-visible AND a dead-strip root, so export every C-ABI symbol the
  # Dart bindings look up (wire_*/new_*/drop_*/…), derived from the archive
  # itself so the list stays in sync with the vendored package. Without this
  # the Release/TestFlight binary boots to a white screen. SRCROOT is the
  # macos/ directory, so ../../ walks up to the repo root where vendor/ lives.
  macos_slice = '$(SRCROOT)/../../vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a'
  macos_archive = File.expand_path('../../vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a', __dir__)
  ffi_symbols = `nm -gU -arch arm64 #{macos_archive}`.lines
    .map(&:split)
    .select { |cols| %w[T D S].include?(cols[1]) && cols[2] }
    .map { |cols| cols[2] }
    .uniq
    .grep(/^_(wire|new|drop|free|get|store|init|inflate|share)_/)
    .sort
  raise "no wasm_run FFI symbols found in #{macos_archive}" if ffi_symbols.empty?
  export_flags = ffi_symbols.map { |s| "-Wl,-exported_symbol,#{s}" }
  installer.aggregate_targets.each do |aggregate_target|
    aggregate_target.user_project.targets.each do |target|
      next unless target.name == 'Runner'
      target.build_configurations.each do |config|
        # Archive/install builds run `strip` per STRIP_STYLE. The default
        # "all" removes the dyld exports trie entirely, which kills the
        # dlsym-based wasm_run lookups at runtime — TestFlight white screen.
        # "non-global" (strip -x) keeps the trie intact.
        config.build_settings['STRIP_STYLE'] = 'non-global'
        ldflags = Array(config.build_settings['OTHER_LDFLAGS'] || ['$(inherited)']).dup
        # Drop stale wasm_run flags from earlier pod installs.
        ldflags.reject! { |f| f == '-force_load' || f.include?('wasm_run_dart.a') || f.start_with?('-Wl,-exported_symbol,') }
        ldflags << "-Wl,-force_load,#{macos_slice}"
        # Debug must NOT get -exported_symbol flags: giving any flips ld
        # into "export only these" mode, which hides the JIT entry point
        # (main) from the debug host — abort_could_not_find_entry_point
        # at launch. Debug exports all globals by default, so dlsym finds
        # the wire_* symbols without any flags.
        ldflags.concat(export_flags) unless config.name == 'Debug'
        config.build_settings['OTHER_LDFLAGS'] = ldflags
      end
    end
    aggregate_target.user_project.save
  end

  This library contains the necessary platform bindings for executing `package:wasm_run`'s Web Assembly executor.
  Uses Rust's wasmtime optimizing runtime or wasmi interpreter.
version: 0.1.0
homepage: https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run

topics:
  - wasm
  - interop
  - runtime
  - interpreter
  - ffi

environment:
  sdk: ">=2.19.0 <4.0.0"
  flutter: ">=2.11.0"

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter
  plugin_platform_interface: ^2.0.2
  flutter_web_plugins:
    sdk: flutter
  wasm_run: ^0.1.0

dev_dependencies:
  ffi: ^2.0.1
  ffigen: ">=8.0.0 <10.0.0"
  very_good_analysis: ^5.0.0

# For information on the generic Dart part of this file, see the
# following page: https://dart.dev/tools/pub/pubspec

# The following section is specific to Flutter packages.
flutter:
  # This section identifies this Flutter project as a plugin project.
  # The 'pluginClass' specifies the class (in Java, Kotlin, Swift, Objective-C, etc.)
  # which should be registered in the plugin registry. This is required for
  # using method channels.
  # The Android 'package' specifies package in which the registered class is.
  # This is required for using method channels on Android.
  # The 'ffiPlugin' specifies that native code should be built and bundled.
  # This is required for using `dart:ffi`.
  # All these are used by the tooling to maintain consistency when
  # adding or updating assets for this project.
  #
  # Please refer to README.md for a detailed explanation.
  plugin:
    platforms:
      android:
        ffiPlugin: true
        dartPluginClass: WasmRunFlutterNative
      ios:
        ffiPlugin: true
        dartPluginClass: WasmRunFlutterNative
      linux:
        ffiPlugin: true
        dartPluginClass: WasmRunFlutterNative
      macos:
        ffiPlugin: true
        dartPluginClass: WasmRunFlutterNative
      windows:
        ffiPlugin: true
        dartPluginClass: WasmRunFlutterNative
      # NOTE (Flutter Agent Harness fork): the web platform entry was removed.
      # The flutter_rust_bridge 1.x generated bindings in package:wasm_run
      # import dart:ffi unconditionally, which cannot compile for the web;
      # registering the web plugin broke `flutter build web` for consumers.
      # Web support would require regenerating the bindings with a newer
      # generator (which broke the native build), so apps must fall back to a
      # pure-Dart implementation in the browser.

  # To add assets to your plugin package, add an assets section, like this:

  #   - images/a_dot_ham.jpeg

  # For details regarding assets in packages, see

  #
  # An image asset can refer to one or more resolution-specific "variants", see

  # To add custom fonts to your plugin package, add a fonts section here,

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):

Pod::Spec.new do |s|
  s.name          = 'wasm_run_flutter'
  s.version       = '0.0.1'
  s.summary       = 'iOS/macOS Flutter bindings for wasm_run'
  s.license       = { :file => '../LICENSE' }
  s.homepage      = 'https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run'
  s.authors       = { 'Juan Manuel Castillo' => '42351046+juancastillo0@users.noreply.github.com' }

  # This will ensure the source files in Classes/ are included in the native
  # builds of apps using this FFI plugin. Podspec does not support relative
  # paths, so Classes contains a forwarder C file that relatively imports
  # `../src/*` so that the C sources can be shared among all target platforms.
  s.source              = { :path => '.' }
  s.source_files        = 'Classes/**/*'
  s.public_header_files = 'Classes/**/*.h'
  # No s.vendored_frameworks (#1096 AC4): the macOS app resolves the
  # wasm_run FFI surface via dlsym on its OWN executable — Runner.xcodeproj
  # force_loads WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a
  # and exports the _wire_* symbols (CI verifies them per build). The
  # embedded dynamic wasm_run_flutter.framework (27 MB unpacked) was a
  # never-loaded fallback; vendoring it here is what put it in
  # Frameworks/. The XCFramework download block above STAYS — the static
  # archive inside it feeds the force_load and the Podfile symbol check.

  s.ios.deployment_target = '11.0'
  s.osx.deployment_target = '10.13'
end

running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1227
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1227
- **Title**: feat(1096): mac size diet — wasm_run_flutter.framework + never-loaded assets, ratcheted
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1096-size-diet` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +48
- **Deletions**: -28
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T13:54:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T14:17:29Z

## PR Description

Part of #1096 — slice 2: the cuts slice 1 explicitly deferred (AC4 + direction-3 analog on macOS, owner-decision items untouched). Budget-gate script unchanged; baselines reseeded onto the measured post-cut shape.

## Delivered

### AC4 — macOS app ships without `wasm_run_flutter.framework` (27.1 MB unpacked)
`vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/wasm_run_flutter.podspec`: `s.vendored_frameworks` removed. The embedded dynamic framework was a **never-loaded fallback**: the Dart FFI surface resolves via dlsym on the app's own executable — `Runner.xcodeproj` force_loads `WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a` and exports the `_wire_*` symbols (verified per build by the existing `wasm_run FFI symbol verification` step). `createLibraryImpl` (`vendor/wasm_run/lib/src/ffi/io.dart:50-56`) tries `DynamicLibrary.executable()` first on macOS and `_validateLibrary` checks exactly `wire_compile_wasm` — the symbol the CI gate asserts. So `WasmRunLibrary.setUp(override: false)` no-ops on the pruned build; **no Dart change, no boot-time dylib download**. The XCFramework cache/restore/download stays untouched — the static archive feeds the force_load and the Podfile symbol check (`Podfile:132-141`); `wasmrun_restore_budget_test` stays green (5/5).

### macOS flutter_assets diet (direction 3 analog, ~52 MB unpacked)
`build-macos.yml` Package step prunes, **before any codesign**:
- `flutter_assets/assets/wasm` — ~47 MB of WASI interpreter modules loaded exclusively through `WasiSandboxShell` (`env_factory_io.dart` routes desktops to the host `Process` shell; every `rootBundle.load('assets/wasm/…')` lives in the mobile-only shell — re-verified on current main). Mobile (iOS/Android) builds untouched — they keep the full set (backward-compat invariant).
- `flutter_assets/packages/js_widget_runtime/test` — 5.6 MB coach_anny.glb test fixture of the pub package, declared as package assets; nothing in the app references that path (grep over flutter_app/lib, packages, lib, bundled JS apps).

### Same fixture prune on every other shipped web shape (5.6 MB each)
`scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` (extension zip), `.github/workflows/pages.yml` (fa1.dev), `scripts/build_office_addin.sh` (outlook pane).

### AC1 ratchet — baselines reseeded onto the post-cut shape
Both `scripts/size_budget` floors rewritten from the **real v1.0.504 release artifacts** with the cuts applied (`--reseed`; script unchanged):
- mac zip: TOTAL 203,341,721 → 111,001,004 B unpacked (**−45.3%**); compressed auto-update zip 75.8 MB → 41.0 MB (**−46%**). DMG shrinks identically.
- extension: TOTAL 78,149,373 → 72,527,489 B (**−7.1%**); compressed 28.3 → 26.4 MB.

Gate proofs (all against the committed floors):
- cut mac zip vs pre-PR baseline: PASS (TOTAL −45.3%, no line grew) — the cut ships green even before the reseed lands
- pre-cut v1.0.504 mac zip vs new floor: **FAIL** — 4 NEW >5% lines (`wasm_run_flutter.framework` 27.1 MB, `python.wasm` 30.4 MB, `coreutils.wasm` 8.4 MB, `coach_anny.glb` 5.6 MB), TOTAL +83.2%
- pre-cut extension vs new floor: **FAIL** — glb NEW >5%, TOTAL +7.8%
- tampered cut zip (main binary +10%): **FAIL** (GREW)
- `size_manifest.py selftest`: 11/11 PASS
- per-line shapes of both cut zips otherwise byte-identical to the shipped releases (only the cut lines + engine-bump drift between v1.0.493 baselines and v1.0.504)

### Not needed (verified, deliberately no diff)
- No `wasm_setup_io.dart` change: with the framework gone, `setUp(override:false)` → `isReachable()` → `executable()` succeeds (static link + exported symbols, CI-gated) → early return. The download path never runs on release or dev builds (force_load applies to both).
- iOS podspec untouched — iOS vendors its own framework slice and statically links it.

## Remaining (owner decisions / later slices, unchanged from the issue)
- AC5: iOS lite flavor vs accept-35 MB (LiteRT/Gemma on-device stack, 35 MB iOS / 45 MB macOS)
- OQ3: `--wasm` (skwasm) spike; App.framework 89–92 MB code-size audit (direction 6)
- mac canvaskit rev-dir inner mirror (web-only shape; needs network trace before cutting — extension/web floors already carry it)
- Known gate floor: NEW-line share is 5% of TOTAL — a future single line under that (e.g. a small asset) regrows silently; the TOTAL line still covers aggregate drift.

## CI note
Per fleet policy this PR does not dispatch or rerun workflows; SM schedules CI.

  dmtools list                           # List available MCP tools

  dmtools <tool> [args...]              # Execute MCP tool with args
  dmtools <tool> --data '{"json"}'      # Execute with inline JSON
  dmtools <tool> --file params.json     # Execute with JSON file
  dmtools <tool> --verbose              # Execute with verbose output
  dmtools <tool> --debug                # Execute with debug output and error messages
  dmtools <tool> <<EOF                  # Execute with heredoc
  {"json": "data"}
  EOF

Examples:
  dmtools list
  dmtools doctor
  dmtools run job-config.json
  dmtools run codegenerator --param1 test
  dmtools jira_get_ticket DMC-479 summary,description
  dmtools jira_get_ticket --data '{"key": "DMC-479", "fields": ["summary"]}'

Environment Variables:
  DMTOOLS_INTEGRATIONS    Comma-separated list of integrations (jira,confluence,figma)

  The tool automatically loads environment variables from dmtools.env

      next unless target.name == 'Runner'
      target.build_configurations.each do |config|
        # Archive/install builds run `strip` per STRIP_STYLE. The default
        # "all" removes the dyld exports trie entirely, which kills the
        # dlsym-based wasm_run lookups at runtime — TestFlight white screen.
        # "non-global" (strip -x) keeps the trie intact.
        config.build_settings['STRIP_STYLE'] = 'non-global'
        ldflags = Array(config.build_settings['OTHER_LDFLAGS'] || ['$(inherited)']).dup
        # Drop stale wasm_run flags from earlier pod installs.
        ldflags.reject! { |f| f == '-force_load' || f.include?('wasm_run_dart.a') || f.start_with?('-Wl,-exported_symbol,') }
        ldflags << "-Wl,-force_load,#{macos_slice}"
        # Debug must NOT get -exported_symbol flags: giving any flips ld
        # into "export only these" mode, which hides the JIT entry point
        # (main) from the debug host — abort_could_not_find_entry_point
        # at launch. Debug exports all globals by default, so dlsym finds
        # the wire_* symbols without any flags.
        ldflags.concat(export_flags) unless config.name == 'Debug'
        config.build_settings['OTHER_LDFLAGS'] = ldflags
      end
    end
    aggregate_target.user_project.save
  end
end

  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.

    worktrees behind.

## PR Description

Part of #1096 — slice 2: the cuts slice 1 explicitly deferred (AC4 + direction-3 analog on macOS, owner-decision items untouched). Budget-gate script unchanged; baselines reseeded onto the measured post-cut shape.

## Delivered

### AC4 — macOS app ships without `wasm_run_flutter.framework` (27.1 MB unpacked)
`vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/wasm_run_flutter.podspec`: `s.vendored_frameworks` removed. The embedded dynamic framework was a **never-loaded fallback**: the Dart FFI surface resolves via dlsym on the app's own executable — `Runner.xcodeproj` force_loads `WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a` and exports the `_wire_*` symbols (verified per build by the existing `wasm_run FFI symbol verification` step). `createLibraryImpl` (`vendor/wasm_run/lib/src/ffi/io.dart:50-56`) tries `DynamicLibrary.executable()` first on macOS and `_validateLibrary` checks exactly `wire_compile_wasm` — the symbol the CI gate asserts. So `WasmRunLibrary.setUp(override: false)` no-ops on the pruned build; **no Dart change, no boot-time dylib download**. The XCFramework cache/restore/download stays untouched — the static archive feeds the force_load and the Podfile symbol check (`Podfile:132-141`); `wasmrun_restore_budget_test` stays green (5/5).

### macOS flutter_assets diet (direction 3 analog, ~52 MB unpacked)
`build-macos.yml` Package step prunes, **before any codesign**:
- `flutter_assets/assets/wasm` — ~47 MB of WASI interpreter modules loaded exclusively through `WasiSandboxShell` (`env_factory_io.dart` routes desktops to the host `Process` shell; every `rootBundle.load('assets/wasm/…')` lives in the mobile-only shell — re-verified on current main). Mobile (iOS/Android) builds untouched — they keep the full set (backward-compat invariant).
- `flutter_assets/packages/js_widget_runtime/test` — 5.6 MB coach_anny.glb test fixture of the pub package, declared as package assets; nothing in the app references that path (grep over flutter_app/lib, packages, lib, bundled JS apps).

### Same fixture prune on every other shipped web shape (5.6 MB each)
`scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` (extension zip), `.github/workflows/pages.yml` (fa1.dev), `scripts/build_office_addin.sh` (outlook pane).

### AC1 ratchet — baselines reseeded onto the post-cut shape
Both `scripts/size_budget` floors rewritten from the **real v1.0.504 release artifacts** with the cuts applied (`--reseed`; script unchanged):
- mac zip: TOTAL 203,341,721 → 111,001,004 B unpacked (**−45.3%**); compressed auto-update zip 75.8 MB → 41.0 MB (**−46%**). DMG shrinks identically.
- extension: TOTAL 78,149,373 → 72,527,489 B (**−7.1%**); compressed 28.3 → 26.4 MB.

Gate proofs (all against the committed floors):
- cut mac zip vs pre-PR baseline: PASS (TOTAL −45.3%, no line grew) — the cut ships green even before the reseed lands
- pre-cut v1.0.504 mac zip vs new floor: **FAIL** — 4 NEW >5% lines (`wasm_run_flutter.framework` 27.1 MB, `python.wasm` 30.4 MB, `coreutils.wasm` 8.4 MB, `coach_anny.glb` 5.6 MB), TOTAL +83.2%
- pre-cut extension vs new floor: **FAIL** — glb NEW >5%, TOTAL +7.8%
- tampered cut zip (main binary +10%): **FAIL** (GREW)
- `size_manifest.py selftest`: 11/11 PASS
- per-line shapes of both cut zips otherwise byte-identical to the shipped releases (only the cut lines + engine-bump drift between v1.0.493 baselines and v1.0.504)

### Not needed (verified, deliberately no diff)
- No `wasm_setup_io.dart` change: with the framework gone, `setUp(override:false)` → `isReachable()` → `executable()` succeeds (static link + exported symbols, CI-gated) → early return. The download path never runs on release or dev builds (force_load applies to both).
- iOS podspec untouched — iOS vendors its own framework slice and statically links it.

## Remaining (owner decisions / later slices, unchanged from the issue)
- AC5: iOS lite flavor vs accept-35 MB (LiteRT/Gemma on-device stack, 35 MB iOS / 45 MB macOS)
- OQ3: `--wasm` (skwasm) spike; App.framework 89–92 MB code-size audit (direction 6)
- mac canvaskit rev-dir inner mirror (web-only shape; needs network trace before cutting — extension/web floors already carry it)
- Known gate floor: NEW-line share is 5% of TOTAL — a future single line under that (e.g. a small asset) regrows silently; the TOTAL line still covers aggregate drift.

## CI note
Per fleet policy this PR does not dispatch or rerun workflows; SM schedules CI.

  dmtools <tool> --data '{"json"}'      # Execute with inline JSON
  dmtools <tool> --file params.json     # Execute with JSON file
  dmtools <tool> --verbose              # Execute with verbose output
  dmtools <tool> --debug                # Execute with debug output and error messages
  dmtools <tool> <<EOF                  # Execute with heredoc
  {"json": "data"}
  EOF

Examples:
  dmtools list
  dmtools doctor
  dmtools run job-config.json
  dmtools run codegenerator --param1 test
  dmtools jira_get_ticket DMC-479 summary,description
  dmtools jira_get_ticket --data '{"key": "DMC-479", "fields": ["summary"]}'

Environment Variables:
  DMTOOLS_INTEGRATIONS    Comma-separated list of integrations (jira,confluence,figma)

  The tool automatically loads environment variables from dmtools.env

The issue: `EnforceBundling.swift` calls `dummy_method_to_enforce_bundling()` — a C function defined in the static library (`libwasm_run_dart.a`), and also references a huge list of FRB symbols (`_drop_dart_object`, `_inflate_*`, `_new_*`, `_wire_*` presumably in the rest of the list). Previously the pod target linked the vendored framework (dynamic), which satisfied these symbols in the pod target itself. Now that `s.vendored_frameworks` is removed, the pod target builds `EnforceBundling.o` but nothing links the static archive into the pod target, so the pod target's link fails with undefined symbols.

Where do these symbols come from? The static archive `WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a` contains `dummy_method_to_enforce_bundling` and the frb-generated symbols. The app target force_loads that archive and exports the symbols (via `-Wl,-exported_symbol` or `FORCE_LOAD` linker flags in Runner.xcodeproj / xcconfig). At runtime, `DynamicLibrary.executable()` resolves them.

But the pod target (wasm_run_flutter.framework, a dynamic framework target built by Pods.xcodeproj) compiles EnforceBundling.swift which references the symbols at link time. With the vendored framework removed, the pod target has no source of those symbols → link error.

The iOS podspec keeps `s.vendored_frameworks` (and iOS statically links it — building the framework's code into the app). The macOS one removed it entirely, so the pod target's EnforceBundling.swift (which references ~200 FRB symbols + dummy_method_to_enforce_bundling from the static archive) no longer links.

Wait — but did the macOS podspec's EnforceBundling compile before? Yes — it linked against the vendored dynamic framework which contained those symbols.

Now what's the right fix consistent with the PR's intent (drop the 27 MB framework from the shipped app, keep FFI working via dlsym on executable with force-loaded static archive)?

Options:

**Option A**: Keep the pod target compiling by linking the static archive into the pod target instead of vendoring the framework: `s.vendored_libraries = "Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a"`. But that would statically link all frb symbols into the pod framework — and the pod framework would still be shipped (it's a source-built framework from source_files, tiny — just EnforceBundling). Hmm, but then the framework would export duplicate symbols of the force-loaded app archive. Duplicates between app executable and dylib are fine at runtime (two-level namespace, app exports take precedence for dlsym on executable? Actually dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT) searches... DynamicLibrary.executable() looks up in the executable's exported symbols table. Duplicates in a dylib don't break that). But it does duplicate code into the shipped framework (small-ish? the static archive is how big? 27MB dynamic framework included the rust static lib; the archive likely several MB). That defeats the size diet partially.

**Option B**: Remove EnforceBundling from the macOS plugin build. Why does EnforceBundling exist? It's the standard flutter_rust_bridge pattern: dummy method referencing all generated symbols so the linker doesn't strip them. On iOS it matters because the static archive is linked into the app and dead-code elimination might strip unused wire symbols. On macOS, the app force_loads the whole archive and exports _wire_* symbols, so the dummy isn't needed. If the pod target has no source files... but a pod with no source_files may fail. Actually the plugin also has frb.h header (public_header_files). Could set s.source_files to nothing meaningful? Pods require at least something? Actually a podspec with empty source_files might be OK (resource-less pod). But the header is public API... The header is included via package's ffi? The Dart side uses DynamicLibrary directly, not the plugin's C API. The Classes/frb.h is the C header for ffigen on the Dart side maybe.

Hmm — but wait, does the Runner force_load + export only apply to Release? The PR says force_load applies to release and dev builds. Let me check the Runner.xcodeproj and Podfile to understand the linking setup, and how the symbols get exported. Also check the "wasm_run FFI symbol verification" CI step.

**Option C**: Make the podspec not build EnforceBundling on macOS: move EnforceBundling.swift out of macos/Classes (it's in macos/Classes). The ios podspec has its own Classes dir? ios/ likely has its own Classes with its own EnforceBundling. Let me check.

  # They are referenced only from Dart via dlsym (DynamicLibrary.executable()),
  # so the linker never pulls them in: force_load alone is not enough because

  # code, and dlsym only sees exported symbols. Exporting a symbol makes it
  # both dlsym-visible AND a dead-strip root, so export every C-ABI symbol the
  # Dart bindings look up (wire_*/new_*/drop_*/…), derived from the archive

  # the Release/TestFlight binary boots to a white screen. SRCROOT is the
  # macos/ directory, so ../../ walks up to the repo root where vendor/ lives.

    .map { |cols| cols[2] }

      target.build_configurations.each do |config|

        # "all" removes the dyld exports trie entirely, which kills the
        # dlsym-based wasm_run lookups at runtime — TestFlight white screen.
        # "non-global" (strip -x) keeps the trie intact.
        config.build_settings['STRIP_STYLE'] = 'non-global'
        ldflags = Array(config.build_settings['OTHER_LDFLAGS'] || ['$(inherited)']).dup
        # Drop stale wasm_run flags from earlier pod installs.
        ldflags.reject! { |f| f == '-force_load' || f.include?('wasm_run_dart.a') || f.start_with?('-Wl,-exported_symbol,') }
        ldflags << "-Wl,-force_load,#{macos_slice}"
        # Debug must NOT get -exported_symbol flags: giving any flips ld
        # into "export only these" mode, which hides the JIT entry point
        # (main) from the debug host — abort_could_not_find_entry_point
        # at launch. Debug exports all globals by default, so dlsym finds
        # the wire_* symbols without any flags.
        ldflags.concat(export_flags) unless config.name == 'Debug'
        config.build_settings['OTHER_LDFLAGS'] = ldflags
      end
    end
    aggregate_target.user_project.save
  end

- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for

  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`

    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1227
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1227
- **Title**: feat(1096): mac size diet — wasm_run_flutter.framework + never-loaded assets, ratcheted
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1096-size-diet` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 7
- **Additions**: +48
- **Deletions**: -28
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T13:54:04Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T14:17:29Z

## PR Description

Part of #1096 — slice 2: the cuts slice 1 explicitly deferred (AC4 + direction-3 analog on macOS, owner-decision items untouched). Budget-gate script unchanged; baselines reseeded onto the measured post-cut shape.

## Delivered

### AC4 — macOS app ships without `wasm_run_flutter.framework` (27.1 MB unpacked)
`vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/wasm_run_flutter.podspec`: `s.vendored_frameworks` removed. The embedded dynamic framework was a **never-loaded fallback**: the Dart FFI surface resolves via dlsym on the app's own executable — `Runner.xcodeproj` force_loads `WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a` and exports the `_wire_*` symbols (verified per build by the existing `wasm_run FFI symbol verification` step). `createLibraryImpl` (`vendor/wasm_run/lib/src/ffi/io.dart:50-56`) tries `DynamicLibrary.executable()` first on macOS and `_validateLibrary` checks exactly `wire_compile_wasm` — the symbol the CI gate asserts. So `WasmRunLibrary.setUp(override: false)` no-ops on the pruned build; **no Dart change, no boot-time dylib download**. The XCFramework cache/restore/download stays untouched — the static archive feeds the force_load and the Podfile symbol check (`Podfile:132-141`); `wasmrun_restore_budget_test` stays green (5/5).

### macOS flutter_assets diet (direction 3 analog, ~52 MB unpacked)
`build-macos.yml` Package step prunes, **before any codesign**:
- `flutter_assets/assets/wasm` — ~47 MB of WASI interpreter modules loaded exclusively through `WasiSandboxShell` (`env_factory_io.dart` routes desktops to the host `Process` shell; every `rootBundle.load('assets/wasm/…')` lives in the mobile-only shell — re-verified on current main). Mobile (iOS/Android) builds untouched — they keep the full set (backward-compat invariant).
- `flutter_assets/packages/js_widget_runtime/test` — 5.6 MB coach_anny.glb test fixture of the pub package, declared as package assets; nothing in the app references that path (grep over flutter_app/lib, packages, lib, bundled JS apps).

### Same fixture prune on every other shipped web shape (5.6 MB each)
`scripts/build_browser_ext.sh` (extension zip), `.github/workflows/pages.yml` (fa1.dev), `scripts/build_office_addin.sh` (outlook pane).

### AC1 ratchet — baselines reseeded onto the post-cut shape
Both `scripts/size_budget` floors rewritten from the **real v1.0.504 release artifacts** with the cuts applied (`--reseed`; script unchanged):
- mac zip: TOTAL 203,341,721 → 111,001,004 B unpacked (**−45.3%**); compressed auto-update zip 75.8 MB → 41.0 MB (**−46%**). DMG shrinks identically.
- extension: TOTAL 78,149,373 → 72,527,489 B (**−7.1%**); compressed 28.3 → 26.4 MB.

Gate proofs (all against the committed floors):
- cut mac zip vs pre-PR baseline: PASS (TOTAL −45.3%, no line grew) — the cut ships green even before the reseed lands
- pre-cut v1.0.504 mac zip vs new floor: **FAIL** — 4 NEW >5% lines (`wasm_run_flutter.framework` 27.1 MB, `python.wasm` 30.4 MB, `coreutils.wasm` 8.4 MB, `coach_anny.glb` 5.6 MB), TOTAL +83.2%
- pre-cut extension vs new floor: **FAIL** — glb NEW >5%, TOTAL +7.8%
- tampered cut zip (main binary +10%): **FAIL** (GREW)
- `size_manifest.py selftest`: 11/11 PASS
- per-line shapes of both cut zips otherwise byte-identical to the shipped releases (only the cut lines + engine-bump drift between v1.0.493 baselines and v1.0.504)

### Not needed (verified, deliberately no diff)
- No `wasm_setup_io.dart` change: with the framework gone, `setUp(override:false)` → `isReachable()` → `executable()` succeeds (static link + exported symbols, CI-gated) → early return. The download path never runs on release or dev builds (force_load applies to both).
- iOS podspec untouched — iOS vendors its own framework slice and statically links it.

## Remaining (owner decisions / later slices, unchanged from the issue)
- AC5: iOS lite flavor vs accept-35 MB (LiteRT/Gemma on-device stack, 35 MB iOS / 45 MB macOS)
- OQ3: `--wasm` (skwasm) spike; App.framework 89–92 MB code-size audit (direction 6)
- mac canvaskit rev-dir inner mirror (web-only shape; needs network trace before cutting — extension/web floors already carry it)
- Known gate floor: NEW-line share is 5% of TOTAL — a future single line under that (e.g. a small asset) regrows silently; the TOTAL line still covers aggregate drift.

## CI note
Per fleet policy this PR does not dispatch or rerun workflows; SM schedules CI.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:

  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`

  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)

# Rework: fix red `Build macOS (debug)` leg (Quality gate)

## Issues/Notes

- **CI failure (root cause)**: head `cc81c735` went red on `build-macos` (Quality gate leg `Build macOS (debug)`). The link step of the `wasm_run_flutter` pod target failed with **~200 undefined symbols for architecture arm64** (`_drop_dart_object`, `_inflate_*`, `_new_*`, `_wire_*`, …) referenced from `_dummy_method_to_enforce_bundling in EnforceBundling.o`.
- **Why**: the PR removed `s.vendored_frameworks` from `vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/wasm_run_flutter.podspec` (AC4 — drop the 27 MB never-loaded `wasm_run_flutter.framework`). But `Classes/EnforceBundling.swift` still rode in the macOS pod. Its dummy references the flutter_rust_bridge symbols that **only the removed vendored dynamic framework used to satisfy** at the pod-target link step — so the pod target now links against nothing defining them and the build fails before the app ever links.
- **Why no other fix**: re-vendoring anything (`vendored_frameworks` or `vendored_libraries` on the static archive) would either resurrect the 27 MB framework or statically link the rust archive into the pod framework — recreating the bloat AC4 removed. The pod target also never needed the dummy: the **Runner** target force_loads `libwasm_run_dart.a` and exports every FFI symbol (`flutter_app/macos/Podfile`, non-Debug; Debug exports all globals), and `package:wasm_run` resolves them via `DynamicLibrary.executable()`. `EnforceBundling` is the **iOS** mechanism (app statically links the pod's vendored framework there; the dummy keeps dead-code stripping from discarding the `wire_*` roots) — iOS podspec is untouched.
- **Review threads**: thread 1 (re-enable pointer note) was already resolved before this rework (pointer landed at the rm site in `build-macos.yml`). The only open item is the CI-red notice — fixed by this change.

## Approach

TDD (RED → GREEN → full suite), same static-lint style as the existing `wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` (the failure is link-time on macOS; this Linux runner cannot run `flutter build macos`, so the guard lints the exact invariant the linker enforces):

1. **RED** — added `test/wasmrun_macos_pod_link_test.dart`: fails if the macOS podspec vendors any framework/library, if `macos/Classes/` compiles any source (`.swift`/`.m`/`.c`/…) while doing so, or if the Podfile stops force_loading/exporting the static archive (the provider side). It reproduced the failure: `EnforceBundling.swift` flagged as the offending compiled source.
2. **GREEN** — removed `vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Classes/EnforceBundling.swift` (header-only pod; `frb.h` stays as the public FFI surface so `pod install` materializes the target) and rewrote the podspec comment to document *why*: the header-only macOS pod, where the symbols actually come from (Runner force_load + exported symbols), the iOS-vs-macOS EnforceBundling distinction, and the exact link error this prevents.
3. Verified the podspec still parses (`ruby -c` → Syntax OK) and no remaining reference to `EnforceBundling` exists in the macOS plugin/app.

## Files Modified

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Classes/EnforceBundling.swift` | **Deleted** — iOS-only mechanism; its undefined FFI references broke the pod-target link once the vendored framework was removed |
| `vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/wasm_run_flutter.podspec` | Comment rewritten: documents the header-only macOS pod, the Runner force_load/export symbol source, and the link failure this guards against |
| `test/wasmrun_macos_pod_link_test.dart` | **New** — static lint pinning the linkability invariant (no vendored framework/library; no compiled sources in the macOS pod; Podfile keeps force_load + exported_symbol) |

## Test Coverage

- `test/wasmrun_macos_pod_link_test.dart` — 3/3 PASS (failed 2/3 before the fix, reproducing the exact CI failure mode; the third leg guards the symbol provider).
- `test/wasmrun_restore_budget_test.dart` — 5/5 PASS (unaffected; the XCFramework download block the restore step depends on stays).
- Full test-core suite (`dart test --exclude-tags llm,browser-ext,perf,pty`, same selection CI runs) — see final comment; `dart analyze` clean on the new test; `dart format` applied.

## CI note

Per fleet policy this PR does not dispatch or rerun workflows; the push of this fix produces a new head, which SM validation picks up.

  # wasm_run FFI symbols live in a static library inside WasmRun.xcframework.
  # They are referenced only from Dart via dlsym (DynamicLibrary.executable()),
  # so the linker never pulls them in: force_load alone is not enough because
  # DEAD_CODE_STRIPPING=YES (Release default) still discards the unreferenced
  # code, and dlsym only sees exported symbols. Exporting a symbol makes it
  # both dlsym-visible AND a dead-strip root, so export every C-ABI symbol the
  # Dart bindings look up (wire_*/new_*/drop_*/…), derived from the archive
  # itself so the list stays in sync with the vendored package. Without this
  # the Release/TestFlight binary boots to a white screen. SRCROOT is the
  # macos/ directory, so ../../ walks up to the repo root where vendor/ lives.
  macos_slice = '$(SRCROOT)/../../vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a'
  macos_archive = File.expand_path('../../vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a', __dir__)
  ffi_symbols = `nm -gU -arch arm64 #{macos_archive}`.lines
    .map(&:split)
    .select { |cols| %w[T D S].include?(cols[1]) && cols[2] }
    .map { |cols| cols[2] }
    .uniq
    .grep(/^_(wire|new|drop|free|get|store|init|inflate|share)_/)
    .sort
  raise "no wasm_run FFI symbols found in #{macos_archive}" if ffi_symbols.empty?
  export_flags = ffi_symbols.map { |s| "-Wl,-exported_symbol,#{s}" }
  installer.aggregate_targets.each do |aggregate_target|

      target.build_configurations.each do |config|

        # "all" removes the dyld exports trie entirely, which kills the
        # dlsym-based wasm_run lookups at runtime — TestFlight white screen.
        # "non-global" (strip -x) keeps the trie intact.
        config.build_settings['STRIP_STYLE'] = 'non-global'
        ldflags = Array(config.build_settings['OTHER_LDFLAGS'] || ['$(inherited)']).dup
        # Drop stale wasm_run flags from earlier pod installs.
        ldflags.reject! { |f| f == '-force_load' || f.include?('wasm_run_dart.a') || f.start_with?('-Wl,-exported_symbol,') }
        ldflags << "-Wl,-force_load,#{macos_slice}"
        # Debug must NOT get -exported_symbol flags: giving any flips ld
        # into "export only these" mode, which hides the JIT entry point
        # (main) from the debug host — abort_could_not_find_entry_point
        # at launch. Debug exports all globals by default, so dlsym finds
        # the wire_* symbols without any flags.
        ldflags.concat(export_flags) unless config.name == 'Debug'
        config.build_settings['OTHER_LDFLAGS'] = ldflags
      end
    end
    aggregate_target.user_project.save

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).

  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),

  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars

  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.

  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call

  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
